title: Salts - 123 school
heading: Salts
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What is a salt?
questions.a: A substance made up of positive and negative ions

questions.q: Which bond holds the ions together in a salt?
questions.a: The ionic bond (attraction between positive and negative ions)

questions.q: Which types of element does a salt usually consist of?
What is the formula of magnesium chloride? (Mg<sup>2+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup>)
What is the formula of aluminium oxide? (Al<sup>3+</sup> and O<sup>2-</sup>)
What is the formula of calcium phosphate? (Ca<sup>2+</sup> and PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3-</sup>)
What is the formula of ammonium sulfate? (NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> and SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2-</sup>)
What is the formula of iron(III) chloride?
What is the name of Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>?
What is the name of KNO<sub>3</sub>?
What is the name of CuSO<sub>4</sub>?
What is the name of Ba(OH)<sub>2</sub>?
What is the name of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>?
What is the charge of the iron ion in FeCl<sub>3</sub>? (Cl<sup>-</sup>)
questions.a: 3+: 3 chloride ions give 3-; so the iron ion is 3+

questions.q: What is the equation for dissolving sodium chloride in water?
What is the equation for dissolving calcium chloride in water?
What is the equation for dissolving aluminium sulfate in water?
What is the equation for dissolving ammonium sulfate in water?
How many moles of ions are released when 1.0 mol of CaCl<sub>2</sub> dissolves?
questions.a: 3.0 mol: 1.0 mol of Ca<sup>2+</sup> and 2.0 mol of Cl<sup>-</sup>: together 3.0 mol

questions.q: A solution of calcium chloride has a concentration of 0.10 mol/L. What is the concentration of Cl<sup>-</sup> in this solution?
questions.a: 0.20 mol/L: for every CaCl<sub>2</sub>, 2 Cl<sup>-</sup> are released: 2 × 0.10 = 0.20 mol/L

questions.q: How many grams of NaCl (M = 58.44 g/mol) are needed for 0.500 L of a 0.10 mol/L solution?
What is a precipitate?
questions.a: A solid that forms when you mix two solutions

questions.q: Why does solid table salt not conduct electricity?
questions.a: The ions are fixed in their places in the lattice

questions.q: Why does a salt solution conduct electricity?
You mix solutions of silver nitrate and sodium chloride. Which substance precipitates? (use BINAS table 45A)
What is the equation of the precipitation reaction of silver ions with chloride ions?
You mix barium chloride solution with sodium sulfate solution. Which substance precipitates? (use BINAS table 45A)
What is the equation of the precipitation reaction in which limescale (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) forms from ions?
You mix solutions of sodium chloride and potassium nitrate. What happens? (use BINAS table 45A)
questions.a: Nothing precipitates, all combinations dissolve well

questions.q: Which salt is poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 45A)
What is the equation of the precipitation reaction of iron(III) ions with hydroxide ions?
What is water of crystallisation?
questions.a: Water that is built into the crystal lattice of a salt

questions.q: Calculate the mass percentage of water of crystallisation in CuSO<sub>4</sub>·5H<sub>2</sub>O. (use BINAS table 99; M(H<sub>2</sub>O) = 18.02 g/mol)
Name two salts from everyday life and their uses.
questions.a: For example table salt (NaCl) for food, limestone (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) in building materials or fertiliser (NH<sub>4</sub>NO<sub>3</sub>) for plants

questions.q: What happens to the ions when a salt melts and why does it then conduct electricity?
questions.a: The ions come loose from their places in the lattice and can move freely, so the molten substance conducts electricity
